title: Graphene‐Analogous Monolayer Boron Pnictides for High‐Mobility Electronics
material: Monolayer hexagonal boron phosphide (h-BP) and boron arsenide (h-BAs) within single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs)
summary: Graphene-analogous monolayer boron pnictides were synthesized for the first time using confined growth within single-walled carbon nanotubes, overcoming ambient instability issues. The h-BP@s-SWCNTs heterostructure demonstrates significantly enhanced carrier mobility through interface engineering and band structure modulation.
findings: h-BP-filled s-SWCNTs heterostructure achieves ~15-fold mobility enhancement compared to pristine s-SWCNTs
Interfacial interactions between host-guest materials in confined space are crucial for stabilizing metastable hexagonal phase boron pnictides
Dirac-like electronic structure enables intrinsically high carrier mobility for next-generation electronics applications
limitations: Hexagonal phase boron pnictides are inherently unstable under ambient and conventional growth conditions
Synthesis accessibility limited to confined growth strategy within SWCNTs

title: Deterministic Patterning and Alignment of Tellurium Quantum Wires Using Nanoscale Templates
application: Quantum transport, quantum dot devices, electronic and quantum technologies
summary: This work demonstrates deterministic patterning and alignment of tellurium quantum wires using nanoscale templates on amorphous substrates. The approach achieves strong alignment of Te atomic chains at sub-20 nm template widths, enabling observation of quantum transport phenomena. Field-effect transistors show conductance plateaus and gate-tunable Coulomb blockade behavior.
findings: Strong alignment of Te atomic chains achieved at template widths below 20 nm with single-crystal structure confirmed by 4D STEM
FETs exhibit well-defined conductance plateaus at 77 K corresponding to individual 1D subband population
Coulomb blockade emerges at 1.7 K with Te channel functioning as a gate-tunable quantum dot
limitations: Scalable synthesis methods previously lacked control over orientation and patterning of Te atomic chains

metrics.name: Template width
metrics.conditions: for strong Te atomic chain alignment

title: Next‐Generation Two‐Dimensional FET Biosensors: Mechanistic Insights, Surface Functionalization Strategies, and Emerging Device Architectures
material: graphene, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), black phosphorus, MXenes
application: biosensors, label-free biomolecular detection, point-of-care diagnostics, wearable applications
summary: This review examines 2D-material-based FET biosensors using graphene, TMDs, black phosphorus, and MXenes for label-free biomolecular detection. It analyzes sensing mechanisms including electrostatic gating and charge transfer, discusses surface functionalization strategies and methods to overcome Debye screening, and reviews emerging device architectures for improved sensitivity and energy efficiency.
findings: Electrostatic gating, charge transfer, Donnan potential, and charge scattering are key sensing mechanisms in 2D FET biosensors
Surface functionalization with aptamer receptors, high-dielectric media, and high-frequency operation can overcome Debye screening limitations
Schottky-barrier, junctionless, split-gate, and tunnel FETs show promise for enhanced sensitivity and energy efficiency
limitations: Challenges in scalability, stability, and reproducibility of 2D FET biosensors remain unresolved
Ongoing debate about the role and limitations of charge transfer in graphene-based systems
Debye screening effect limits sensing performance in conventional configurations

title: Rylene Diimides Featuring Quadruple C─H···(O═C) Locking for High‐Mobility Organic Semiconductors
summary: A novel sila-annulated hexarylene diimide is designed with quadruple C─H···(O═C) hydrogen bonding that enables controlled one-dimensional slipped π─π stacking in organic semiconductors. Single-crystalline transistors demonstrate excellent hole mobility with high transfer integrals, providing design principles for large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon materials.
findings: Quadruple C─H···(O═C) locking between silole and diimide groups enables first 1D slipped π─π stacking in ultra-long rylenes
Single-crystalline OFET hole mobility of 3.08 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and electron mobility of 0.06 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹
Hole transfer integral of 110.08 meV and electron transfer integral of 78.08 meV rationalize superior charge transport
limitations: Electron mobility significantly lower than hole mobility
Design limited to specific peri- and bay-position substitution patterns

title: Rapid and Efficient Organic‐Aqueous Two‐Phase Extraction of High‐Purity Semiconducting Single‐Walled Carbon Nanotubes
summary: This work presents an organic-aqueous two-phase extraction method for rapid purification of semiconducting single-walled carbon nanotubes. The approach combines polymer-assisted sorting with interfacial extraction to remove metallic nanotubes while preserving structural integrity, achieving high purity and yield with significantly reduced processing time.
findings: Purification time reduced from approximately 3 hours to 1 hour compared to conventional multi-cycle methods
Purification yield increased from approximately 2.5% to approximately 6.1%
Transistor arrays from purified sc-SWCNTs show semiconducting purity exceeding 99.9999% based on statistical analysis of approximately 2000 devices
limitations: Method applicability demonstrated on three synthesis routes but broader scalability not fully discussed
Large-scale production feasibility beyond the reported device fabrication scale not addressed

metrics.name: Semiconducting purity
metrics.conditions: transistor arrays from purified sc-SWCNTs, statistical analysis of approximately 2000 devices

title: Emergent Electronic, Spin, and Transport Properties of Bilayer van der Waals Heterostructures from Antimonene, Tellurene, and PtTe2 Monolayers
material: Antimonene, Tellurene, PtTe2 bilayer van der Waals heterostructures
application: Tunneling field-effect transistors, nanoelectronic, optoelectronic, piezoelectric, and spintronic devices
summary: Bilayer van der Waals heterostructures composed of antimonene, tellurene, and PtTe2 monolayers were systematically studied using first-principles calculations. The heterostructures exhibit broken spatial inversion symmetry and strong interlayer hybridization, resulting in reduced bandgaps, pronounced spin splitting, and extraordinary Rashba effects with tunable properties via strain and electric fields.
findings: Sb/PtTe2 bilayer exhibits type-III broken-gap band alignment suitable for TFET applications with pronounced tunneling effects
Rashba coefficients of Sb/Te, Te/PtTe2, and Sb/PtTe2 reach 1.08, 2.89, and 2.85 eV Å respectively, enhanceable to 3.45 eV Å under 6% tensile strain
Carrier mobilities of Sb/Te and Te/PtTe2 heterostructures significantly enhanced up to 10^4 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ with improved optical absorption in visible region
limitations: Study is based on first-principles calculations only; experimental validation not provided
Practical device fabrication and integration challenges of these heterostructures not addressed

title: Mechanical Programming of Carrier Flow by Band-Alignment Inversion in Two-Dimensional Heterostructures
material: WSe2/Zr2CO2 heterostructures, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), transition-metal carbides (MXenes)
summary: Tensile strain can reverse the direction of photogenerated carrier transfer in TMDC/MXene heterostructures by inverting band-edge alignment, while maintaining efficient charge separation. This occurs because strain affects the band edges of weakly ionic TMDCs and strongly ionic MXenes in opposite ways. The mechanism enables mechanical control of carrier flow without degrading charge separation kinetics.
findings: Strain-driven band-alignment inversion reverses both electron and hole transfer directions in WSe2/Zr2CO2 heterostructures
Ultrafast femtosecond charge separation and nanosecond carrier lifetimes are preserved during band-alignment inversion
Opposite orbital responses of TMDCs and MXenes to strain enable the inversion mechanism
limitations: Study relies on nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations without experimental validation
Mechanism demonstrated primarily on one specific heterostructure system (WSe2/Zr2CO2)

title: One-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructure Field-Effect Transistors
material: Single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) encapsulated by boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs)
summary: Field-effect transistors were fabricated using individual one-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures consisting of SWCNTs protected by few-layer BNNTs. Direct comparison on the same nanotube with and without BNNT coating revealed that metallic SWCNTs benefit from enhanced output currents via electrostatic screening, while semiconducting SWCNTs show reduced hysteresis through environmental isolation.
findings: BNNT encapsulation provides excellent electrostatic screening that increases output currents in metallic SWCNTs
BNNT protection reduces hysteresis in semiconducting SWCNTs through environmental isolation
BNNTs act as an effective barrier against harsh environments such as oxygen plasma etching during device fabrication
limitations: Device performance is initially susceptible to environmental degradation due to the atomically thin geometry and large surface area of SWCNTs

title: Revisiting the Schottky-Mott Relation for Metal/Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Interfaces: The Role of Interface Dipoles
summary: The study investigates Fermi-level pinning at metal/TMD interfaces using first-principles calculations and experimental techniques. The research demonstrates that interface dipoles and short-range potentials govern Fermi-level pinning, validating the Schottky-Mott relation through metal effective work function analysis.
findings: Fermi-level pinning is controlled by long-range dipole interactions and extended short-range Lennard-Jones potentials
Metal effective work function serves as a reliable figure of merit for the Schottky-Mott relation in 2D semiconductors
The linear Schottky-Mott relation framework improves predictive capabilities for contact engineering in TMD-based devices
limitations: Study focuses on regimes where material thickness is comparable to interface thickness, which may limit general applicability
High contact resistance remains a significant challenge despite improved understanding of Fermi-level pinning mechanisms

title: Sample-to-Answer Serum Diagnostics System-on-Chip
application: point-of-care protein detection, tumor biomarker diagnostics
summary: A biological detection system-on-chip integrates microfluidic purification with carbon nanotube FET biosensors for ultrasensitive protein analysis in serum samples. The device demonstrates direct detection of tumor biomarkers at extremely low concentrations and achieved 100% diagnostic accuracy on 24 clinical serum samples.
findings: Detected tumor biomarkers in undiluted serum across concentration range of 2 fg/mL to 1 pg/mL
Achieved 100% diagnostic accuracy on 24 clinical serum samples
Platform is scalable for future integration of biosensor arrays and multiplexing capabilities
limitations: Preliminary cohort study with only 24 clinical samples
Multiplexing and advanced fluidic control modules not yet fully integrated

title: Molecular dynamics modeling of bonding two materials by atomic scale friction stir welding at different process parameters
summary: Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to examine atomic-scale friction stir welding of two crystallites at varying tool plunge depths. The study investigated how plunge depth influences heating, material deformation, and mass transfer during the welding process.
findings: Increased plunge depth produces more intense heating and reduces resistance of plasticized metal to tool movement
Mass transfer intensity shows minimal dependence on plunge depth variation
Plunge depth can serve as an additional friction stir welding process control parameter
limitations: Simulations limited to nanosized crystallites, scalability to macroscopic welding unclear
Material composition not specified in abstract

title: Electrostatically defined ZnO quantum devices
application: Quantum electronics, single-electron transistors, spin qubits
summary: This review examines electrostatically defined quantum devices based on ZnO heterostructures, emphasizing quantum dots formed through electrostatic gating. ZnO offers advantages similar to Si, including low nuclear spin density, while maintaining high-quality heterostructure capabilities comparable to GaAs. Recent achievements include 1D and 0D electron confinement with observable quantized transport phenomena.
findings: Quantized conductance steps in 1D channels and Coulomb blockade effects observed in 0D structures of ZnO heterostructures
ZnO heterostructures achieve electron coherence and dimensional control through electrostatic gating techniques comparable to conventional GaAs and Si platforms
Low nuclear spin density in ZnO suppresses hyperfine decoherence, offering advantages for quantum device applications
limitations: Review does not provide quantitative performance metrics or benchmarks comparing ZnO devices to GaAs or Si implementations

title: Impact of Elastic Phonon Dephasing on the Switching Performance of Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Field Effect Transistor
journal: International Journal of Computational Materials Science and Engineering
summary: This work uses non-equilibrium Green's function simulations to study how elastic phonon dephasing affects dual-gate armchair graphene nanoribbon transistors. The analysis compares momentum-conserving and momentum-relaxing scattering regimes and their impact on device switching performance and transport properties.
findings: Momentum-conserving dephasing degrades switching behavior by increasing off-state leakage and worsening subthreshold characteristics
Momentum-relaxing dephasing preserves transistor-like operation with minor performance degradation and maintains energy selectivity
Dephasing mechanisms critically influence transport gap characteristics and are essential for reliable nanoscale transistor design
limitations: Study uses scalar coupling parameter to model phonon dephasing rather than full microscopic scattering mechanisms
Analysis limited to dual-gate AGNR configuration

title: Cryogenic wafer probing below one Kelvin: Characterization of normal-metal Coulomb blockade thermometers at wafer scale
summary: This work demonstrates wafer-scale characterization of normal-metal Coulomb blockade thermometers using a cryogenic wafer prober on 150 mm wafers. The devices can operate as primary thermometers without calibration or as secondary resistance thermometers, achieving on-chip electron temperatures below 700 mK and establishing a high-throughput approach for testing quantum devices at cryogenic temperatures.
findings: On-chip electron temperatures achieved below 700 mK across full 150 mm wafers using wafer-scale characterization
Normal-metal tunnel junction CBTs demonstrate functionality as both primary and secondary thermometers
Cryogenic wafer probing enables high-throughput screening of quantum devices and aluminum-based superconducting circuits
limitations: Traditional cryostat characterization limited by turnover time and sample capacity

title: Probing proximity-induced superconductivity in bilayer graphene using gate-defined quantum dots
application: Spectroscopic probing of proximity-induced superconductivity in van der Waals heterostructures
summary: An all-2D hybrid device combines bilayer graphene with superconducting NbSe₂ using gate-defined quantum dots as local probes. The study demonstrates proximity-induced superconductivity in the graphene channel and tracks how the superconducting gap evolves with distance from the superconductor contact.
findings: Proximity-induced superconducting gap reaches up to 80 μeV in proximitized bilayer graphene
Local density of states remains suppressed over distances exceeding 1 μm, indicating highly ballistic superconducting proximity effect
Gate-tunable quantum dots enable local spectroscopic control and characterization of the proximitized channel
limitations: Gap magnitude and spatial extent may be limited by material quality and interface properties
Study focuses on proximity effects at specific distances from the superconductor-semiconductor interface

metrics.name: Suppression distance of local density of states

title: Highly uniform first-electron position in qubit arrays fabricated on dedicated QSOI(R) 300mm commercial platform
summary: A quantum silicon-on-insulator technology compatible with 300mm CMOS fabrication was developed for scalable quantum computing. The QSOI(R) platform, adapted from 28nm FD-SOI, demonstrates significantly improved device uniformity and reduced variability compared to standard 28nm FD-SOI, with successful quantum dot operation in the few-electron regime.
findings: QSOI(R) technology achieves 69% yield for successful charge detection of the first electron across 377 quantum dots
First electron position dispersion of ±35 mV demonstrates highly uniform electrostatic properties at the wafer level
TCAD simulations validate that device electrostatics behave as expected for the QSOI(R) platform
limitations: 31% failure rate in charge detection of first electron suggests room for further optimization
Measurements performed at sub-2K temperatures, limiting immediate practical applications

metrics.name: First electron position dispersion
metrics.conditions: Over 377 quantum dots, wafer-scale measurements at sub-2K
